items.source_name: National Institute on Aging — Providing Comfort at the End of Life
items.source_locator: Providing Comfort at the End of Life — planning for who should be present, spiritual/cultural wishes, and individualized end-of-life preferences.
items.source_version: NIA page reviewed 2022-11-17; official currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: The client's explicitly stated end-of-life ritual and family-presence preferences should be clarified, documented, and accommodated when safe, lawful, and feasible; stereotyping or deferring discussion is not supported.

items.source_locator: Warnings and Precautions §5.3 Ototoxicity and IV administration information: rapid injection, renal impairment, high doses, and other ototoxic drugs increase hearing-risk concerns.
items.source_version: Current FDA labeling as displayed by DailyMed; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Rapid IV furosemide administration is a recognized ototoxicity risk, particularly with renal impairment; controlled administration and hearing-symptom surveillance are appropriate.

items.source_locator: Warnings and Precautions §§5.3 Impaired Renal Function and 5.5 Hyperkalemia; monitoring of renal function and serum potassium.
items.source_version: Label revised May 2025; current DailyMed version rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Lisinopril can worsen renal function and cause hyperkalemia, making renal-function and potassium monitoring the directly supported priority after initiation or dose change in CKD.

items.source_locator: Warnings/Precautions and Laboratory Tests: nephrotoxicity, azotemia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, and frequent renal-function monitoring.
items.source_version: Current conventional amphotericin B FDA label displayed by DailyMed; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: A rising creatinine with potassium or magnesium loss is consistent with amphotericin-associated renal toxicity and merits close renal/electrolyte review.

items.source_locator: ASPEN PN Care Pathway Step 9 Monitor and Reevaluate Patient and Step 11 PN Quality Improvement Program: maintain glucose control and implement CLABSI infection control as separate safety domains.
items.source_version: ASPEN PN Care Pathway listed as 04.2025 and current on ASPEN 2026 site; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Parenteral nutrition can require active glucose monitoring/management; hyperglycemia is not itself a diagnostic marker of CLABSI, so glycemic management and catheter-infection assessment must remain distinct.

items.source_locator: Section III.F Protective Environment: environmental controls for allogeneic HSCT patients, including excluding fresh/dried flowers and potted plants; food safety follows applicable program guidance.
items.source_version: CDC Isolation Precautions guidance maintained on current site; page currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Fresh/dried flowers and potted plants are excluded from the protective environment for HSCT patients; the source does not justify a universal ban on every raw fruit or vegetable for every neutropenic client.

items.source_locator: Drug Interactions §7.2 CYP2C19 Inhibitors: avoid concomitant omeprazole or esomeprazole because active-metabolite exposure and platelet inhibition are reduced.
items.source_version: Current FDA clopidogrel label displayed by DailyMed; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Omeprazole and esomeprazole are the label-supported PPI interaction concern with clopidogrel; the distractors incorrectly generalize the interaction to other acid-suppressing agents.

items.source_locator: 2020 ASRA Local Anesthetic Systemic Toxicity checklist and recognition/treatment guidance for neurologic or cardiovascular toxicity after local anesthetic exposure.
items.source_version: ASRA 2020 LAST checklist retained as current society emergency guidance; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: The abrupt neurologic symptom complex after local anesthetic exposure is concerning for LAST, which can progress to seizures or cardiovascular collapse and requires rapid escalation.

items.source_locator: Emergency Treatment for an Acute MH Event: stop triggering agents, hyperventilate with 100% oxygen, give IV dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg rapidly, and monitor ETCO2, rigidity, heart rate, and temperature.
items.source_version: MHAUS current crisis recommendations on 2026 site; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Rapid ETCO2 rise, rigidity, tachycardia, and acidosis after succinylcholine fit malignant hyperthermia; dantrolene is the specific treatment named by MHAUS.

items.source_name: CDC — Vaccine Administration: After Giving Vaccine
items.source_locator: Managing Acute Vaccine Reactions — Syncope: most vaccine recipients should be observed for about 15 minutes after vaccination while seated or lying safely.
items.source_version: CDC page published 2025-06-23; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: For a routine adolescent vaccination without a special allergy indication, about 15 minutes of safe observation is the supported practice; universal 30-minute or multi-hour observation is not.

items.source_locator: Drug Interactions §7.5 Foods and Patient Counseling: maintain a normal balanced diet with a consistent amount of vitamin K and avoid drastic dietary changes.
items.source_version: DailyMed warfarin label updated 2024-01-02; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Warfarin teaching emphasizes consistency of vitamin K intake and coordination of major dietary changes with INR management, not elimination or unsupervised vitamin-K dosing.

items.source_locator: Safe Patient Handling hazards and solutions: use appropriate mechanical/assistive equipment and safe-handling programs rather than hazardous manual lifting; equipment must suit the patient and task.
items.source_version: Current OSHA healthcare guidance; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: A device that cannot safely accommodate the client's weight should not be used; appropriately rated equipment and trained staff are the supported safe-handling response.

items.source_name: U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission — Radiation Protection Principles
items.source_locator: Radiation Protection Principles — Time, Distance, and Shielding. Supplementary official requirement: 10 CFR §35.410 safety instruction for personnel caring for hospitalized brachytherapy patients.
items.source_version: Current NRC protection principles and 10 CFR Part 35 requirements rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Minimizing time, maximizing distance when care permits, and using prescribed shielding/procedures are the correct occupational radiation-protection principles for brachytherapy care.

items.source_locator: Fall TIPS three-step patient-centered process: assess individual fall-risk factors, develop a personalized prevention plan, and execute that plan consistently.
items.source_version: AHRQ Fall TIPS current toolkit; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Sedation-related fall risk is best addressed with a personalized multicomponent plan rather than bed rest, unilateral medication discontinuation, or reliance on a bed alarm alone.

items.source_locator: 42 CFR §482.13(e)(10) monitoring and §482.13(e)(12) hospital policy; §482.13(f) contains additional violent/self-destructive restraint requirements including the one-hour face-to-face evaluation.
items.source_version: Current eCFR Title 42 §482.13; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Federal restraint rules require monitoring and policy-based implementation but do not establish one universal q1–2-hour reassessment interval for every nonviolent restraint; context and applicable policy/law matter.

items.source_locator: Section V.A.5.c.i acute-care Contact Precautions for known MDRO colonization/infection and V.A.5.h: no recommendation on when to discontinue Contact Precautions — unresolved issue.
items.source_version: CDC/HICPAC MDRO recommendations maintained on current CDC site; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: CDC supports Contact Precautions for known MDRO colonization/infection in acute care and explicitly classifies the discontinuation point as unresolved; facility infection-prevention policy therefore guides practice.

items.source_name: The Joint Commission — Universal Protocol Site Marking FAQ
items.source_locator: Universal Protocol Site Marking FAQ 000001461: accountable licensed practitioner marks the site; limited defined delegation; involve the patient when possible.
items.source_version: Joint Commission FAQ first published 2026-03-04 and updated 2026-03-03; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: The accountable licensed practitioner, with only defined delegation and patient involvement when possible, is the supported site-marking approach when documentation conflicts.

items.source_locator: Workplace Violence hazards and controls: management commitment, worksite analysis, hazard prevention/control, training, recordkeeping, and controls for risks such as isolated work and poor environmental design.
items.source_version: Current OSHA Hospitals eTool; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: A comprehensive prevention program with hazard assessment, training, reporting, security/environmental controls, and reduction of isolated work aligns with OSHA's prevention framework.

items.source_locator: Hazard Communication and hazardous-chemical response: labels/SDS access, employee training, hazard identification, and appropriate protective procedures under 29 CFR 1910.1200.
items.source_version: Current OSHA Hospitals eTool and Hazard Communication requirements; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: An unfamiliar spill should be isolated/managed through trained facility procedures after hazard identification and SDS review; untrained bare-handed cleanup or automatic whole-building evacuation is not universally appropriate.

items.source_locator: AONL Nurse Leader Core Competencies: communication/relationship management, leadership, professionalism, knowledge of the health care environment, business skills, staff development, collaboration, and systems influence.
items.source_version: AONL competency framework current with 2025 updates and 2026 functional-behavior revision activity; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Shared direction, staff participation, development, and connection of improvement work to meaningful outcomes align with current nurse-leader competencies; the item was corrected so it no longer attributes a specific leadership-theory definition to this source.

items.source_locator: TeamSTEPPS 3.0 Mutual Support — DESC: Describe the situation, Express concerns, Suggest alternatives, state Consequences; use constructive discussion to resolve conflict.
items.source_version: AHRQ TeamSTEPPS 3.0 page last reviewed July 2023; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: A structured collaborative discussion that surfaces both nurses' evidence and produces one patient-centered plan is preferable to avoidance, hierarchy alone, or premature discipline.

items.source_name: American Nurses Association — The Nursing Process
items.source_locator: ANA Nursing Process: Assessment, Diagnosis, Outcomes/Planning, Implementation, Evaluation; diagnosis follows analysis of assessment data.
items.source_version: Current ANA nursing-process framework; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: After assessment, the nurse analyzes data to identify nursing problems/diagnoses before outcomes, planning, implementation, and evaluation.

items.source_name: AHRQ Effective Health Care Program — Methods Guide
items.source_locator: Methods Guide — focusing/refining research questions; Tables 6–7 define PICOTS parameters and emphasize a clear, transparent focused question before evidence synthesis.
items.source_version: AHRQ EHC Methods Guide is a maintained living methods resource; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: A focused clinical/practice question should define the problem and desired outcome before the evidence search and practice change; anecdotal protocol copying or implementation-first approaches are not evidence-based.

items.source_locator: TeamSTEPPS 3.0 introduction: communication, team leadership, situation monitoring, and mutual support around patient-centered team performance, with patients/families as team members.
items.source_version: AHRQ TeamSTEPPS 3.0 currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Coordinating disciplines around shared patient-centered goals while each contributes expertise and the client participates is consistent with effective interprofessional teamwork.

items.source_name: HRSA / OPTN — Ethics of Deceased Organ Donor Recovery
items.source_locator: Authorization/Explicit Consent and U.S. Donation Model discussion: first-person authorization is the individual's anatomical gift; surrogate authorization applies when the individual's authorization is absent.
items.source_version: Official HRSA/OPTN ethics resource retained as current; foundational report 2016, currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Documented first-person donor authorization is generally honored through the OPO/legal donation process rather than replaced by bedside family reauthorization.

items.source_locator: HCAHPS Overview/About the Survey: national standardized publicly reported patient-experience survey and current domains such as communication, responsiveness, care coordination, environment, discharge information, and overall rating.
items.source_version: CMS current HCAHPS program with 2025 instrument/content updates; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: HCAHPS measures standardized patient-reported hospital experience domains, not direct mortality/readmission outcomes, staff satisfaction, or billing accuracy.

items.source_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan — NCJMM Recognize Cues, Prioritize Hypotheses, and Take Action based on urgency, likelihood, risk, difficulty, and time constraints.
items.source_version: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: New stridor with increasing work of breathing is the immediate airway threat and appropriately outranks routine teaching, sleep medication, or stable chronic pain.

items.source_name: American Academy of Pediatrics / HealthyChildren — Febrile Seizures
items.source_locator: Febrile Seizures — seizure first aid: protect from injury, position safely/side as appropriate, do not put objects in the mouth, and seek emergency help for prolonged seizure or breathing concern.
items.source_version: AAP HealthyChildren page last updated 2025-12-05; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: After the shaking stops, a drowsy child needs airway/breathing assessment and safe recovery positioning; oral fluids, restraint, or placing objects in the mouth are unsafe.

items.source_name: American Academy of Pediatrics / HealthyChildren — Croup
items.source_locator: Croup in Young Children — stridor at rest, retractions/increasing work of breathing, fatigue/cyanosis, or inability to speak/drink are signs requiring prompt evaluation.
items.source_version: AAP HealthyChildren page last updated 2024-05-10; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Stridor at rest with retractions or increasing fatigue indicates more severe upper-airway obstruction and merits urgent evaluation; mild barky cough/hoarseness without distress does not.

items.source_name: World Society of Emergency Surgery — 2020 Jerusalem Appendicitis Guidelines
items.source_locator: 2020 WSES Jerusalem Guidelines — Topic 1 diagnosis, Statement/Recommendation 1.1 and diagnostic sections describing clinical features, scores, and imaging in suspected acute appendicitis.
items.source_version: Published 2020-04-15; WSES guideline currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Migration of pain from the periumbilical region to the right lower quadrant with focal tenderness and fever is compatible with appendicitis and warrants prompt evaluation; the item does not claim symptoms alone prove the diagnosis.

items.source_name: ESC — 2025 Guidelines for Myocarditis and Pericarditis
items.source_locator: 2025 ESC Guideline §§4.5.4 and 11.8 Cardiac Tamponade: hypotension, raised JVP/neck-vein distention, and muffled/quiet heart sounds; after cardiac surgery effusions may be loculated and cause tamponade.
items.source_version: 2025 ESC Clinical Practice Guideline; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Post-cardiac-surgery hypotension with jugular venous distention and muffled heart sounds is the classic high-risk tamponade pattern and warrants immediate escalation.

items.source_name: ISTH SSC — Updated DIC Definition and Scoring 2025
items.source_locator: ISTH SSC Communication, revised DIC definition: systemic coagulation activation, dysregulated fibrinolysis and endothelial injury causing microthrombosis, with advanced disease producing hemorrhage and/or organ dysfunction.
items.source_version: J Thromb Haemost. 2025;23(7):2356-2362. DOI 10.1016/j.jtha.2025.03.038; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: DIC directly explains simultaneous microthrombosis and bleeding/oozing in severe sepsis; isolated thrombocytopenia or vitamin-K deficiency does not match the systemic microthrombotic-consumptive pattern.

items.source_locator: Signs and Symptoms of Rhabdomyolysis: muscle pain/weakness, dark urine, CK testing, and urgent evaluation; rhabdomyolysis can lead to kidney injury and dangerous electrolyte/cardiac complications.
items.source_version: CDC/NIOSH page published 2025-01-14; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Crush injury with muscle pain, dark urine and markedly elevated CK is rhabdomyolysis; renal function, urine output and potassium are high-priority monitoring targets because AKI and hyperkalemic arrhythmia are major complications.

items.source_name: Endocrine Society — Hypercalcemia of Malignancy Clinical Practice Guideline
items.source_locator: Guideline Introduction — hypercalcemia severity categories (moderate 12–14 mg/dL) and manifestations including constipation, cognitive dysfunction, polyuria/polydipsia, dehydration and renal complications; used here for hypercalcemia manifestations/severity, not to infer malignancy.
items.source_version: J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2023;108(3):507-528; DOI 10.1210/clinem/dgac621; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Calcium 12.8 mg/dL with constipation, thirst and new confusion is compatible with symptomatic hypercalcemia and warrants prompt severity/etiology/hydration/complication assessment; the item does not infer a single cause.

items.source_locator: Indications and Usage and resuscitation precautions: complete/partial reversal of opioid-induced CNS/respiratory depression; establish/support ventilation and repeat dosing/monitoring when required.
items.source_version: Current FDA naloxone label displayed by DailyMed; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: A difficult-to-arouse postoperative patient breathing 8/min after opioids has clinically significant opioid respiratory/CNS depression; withhold opioid, support ventilation, escalate, and prepare/administer naloxone per protocol.

items.source_locator: KDIGO 2024 CKD Guideline: GFR assessment limitations when creatinine is affected by low muscle mass; Chapter 4 Practice Points 4.2.1–4.2.5 on drug dosing, eGFR, cystatin C, and measured GFR when greater accuracy is required.
items.source_version: KDIGO 2024 CKD Guideline remains the current global standard; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Low muscle mass can make serum creatinine alone misleading. Renally cleared medication dosing should use drug-specific renal guidance and an appropriate kidney-function estimate, with cystatin-C or measured GFR considered when creatinine-based estimates are unreliable and accuracy matters.

items.source_name: NLM MedlinePlus — Prothrombin Time and INR
items.source_locator: PT/INR test overview and abnormal-result interpretation: evaluates clotting time and is used for coagulation disorders, liver problems, vitamin-K deficiency and warfarin monitoring.
items.source_version: Current U.S. National Library of Medicine patient/laboratory reference; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: A markedly prolonged PT reflects an abnormality in the extrinsic/common clotting pathway context and can occur with vitamin-K deficiency, liver dysfunction or factor abnormalities; it is not a direct platelet, RBC, or intrinsic-pathway test.

items.source_locator: CRP test overview/results: CRP rises with inflammation from infection, injury, autoimmune and other inflammatory states; the test does not identify the cause or location by itself.
items.source_version: Current U.S. National Library of Medicine laboratory reference; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: CRP is a nonspecific inflammation marker and cannot identify a specific organism or diagnosis without the wider clinical picture.

items.source_name: American Diabetes Association — Standards of Care in Diabetes 2026, Section 6
items.source_locator: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026, Section 6 Glycemic Goals: Recommendations 6.3a–6.9 and goal tables; A1C <7% is appropriate for many nonpregnant adults with individualized targets.
items.source_version: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026, Diabetes Care 49(Suppl 1); currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: A1C 9.5% is well above the usual goal for many nonpregnant adults, while the appropriate treatment target remains individualized to comorbidity, function, preferences, treatment burden and hypoglycemia risk.

items.source_locator: Adult BMI Categories table: BMI 30.0 to <35.0 kg/m² is Class 1 obesity; BMI is a screening measure to interpret with other health information.
items.source_version: CDC page published 2024-03-19; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: BMI 32 kg/m² is in the adult Class 1 obesity screening category, but BMI alone does not establish metabolic disease severity or overall health.

items.source_locator: Fall TIPS patient-centered process: identify individual fall-risk factors, develop a personalized prevention plan, and update/execute the plan as risk changes.
items.source_version: AHRQ Fall TIPS current toolkit; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: A higher Morse score signals risk but does not replace individualized prevention or reassessment; interventions should target the patient's modifiable risk factors and change with clinical status.

items.source_locator: Walking/Gait Belts with Handles: gait belts may stabilize ambulatory patients who can bear some weight; they are not lifting devices and should be used within safe-patient-handling practice.
items.source_version: Current OSHA Hospitals eTool; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: For a weight-bearing but mildly unsteady patient, a properly fitted gait belt used beside the client is safer than improvised sheets, axillary pulling, or having the patient hang from staff.

items.source_name: NCBI Bookshelf / Open RN — Nursing Fundamentals, 2nd ed.
items.source_locator: Nursing Fundamentals, 2nd ed. (Open RN), Mobility/Range-of-Motion section: active, passive, and active-assisted ROM definitions and use.
items.source_version: Open RN Nursing Fundamentals, 2nd ed., 2024; exact NCBI Bookshelf chapter rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Active-assisted ROM means the patient actively initiates movement and receives help to complete the available/prescribed range; active and passive ROM distractors reverse who supplies the movement.

items.source_name: WOCN — Peristomal Skin Assessment Guide for Consumers
items.source_locator: Peristomal moisture-associated skin damage / irritant dermatitis guidance: measure the stoma, fit the barrier opening closely around the base, and change the pouching system promptly for leakage, burning, or itching.
items.source_version: Current WOCN consumer peristomal-skin guide; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Repeated leakage and burning indicate effluent exposure risk; remeasure the stoma, fit the barrier closely, and change a leaking system promptly rather than oversizing, lubricating under the seal, or leaving leakage in place.

items.source_locator: Denture Care and Maintenance: clean dentures daily with nonabrasive methods, avoid hot/boiling water, and keep dentures moist in water or appropriate solution when not worn.
items.source_version: Current ADA oral-health guidance; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Nonabrasive cleaning, avoiding heat that can warp dentures, and moist storage are the supported care practices; abrasive toothpaste, hot water, and dry storage are not.

items.source_name: American Academy of Dermatology — Sunscreen Labels and Sun Protection
items.source_locator: AAD sun-protection guidance: broad-spectrum UVA/UVB, SPF 30 or higher, water resistance, shade/protective clothing, and reapplication about every two hours and after swimming/sweating as directed.
items.source_version: AAD public guidance updated July 2026; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Layered UV protection with broad-spectrum water-resistant SPF 30+, shade, clothing and appropriate reapplication is supported for all skin tones; cloudy days and tanning devices do not remove UV risk.

items.source_name: American Academy of Pediatric Dentistry — Early Childhood Caries Policy
items.source_locator: AAPD Policy on Early Childhood Caries — preventive strategies: establish a dental home within 6 months of first-tooth eruption and no later than 12 months of age.
items.source_version: AAPD Reference Manual 2026–2027; policy latest revision 2025; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Routine preventive dental care should begin with a dental home within six months of first tooth eruption and by 12 months at the latest, not after full dentition, preschool entry, or age three.

items.source_name: CDC/NIOSH — Safe Patient Handling and Mobility
items.source_locator: Safe Patient Handling and Mobility prevention strategies: manual handling is a major musculoskeletal risk; use ergonomic assistive/lifting technology, appropriate devices, and trained programs matched to the patient/task.
items.source_version: CDC/NIOSH page published 2024-05-09; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: A dependent transfer requiring substantial lifting should use appropriate mechanical/assistive technology with trained staff rather than manual lifting justified by body mechanics or staff strength.

items.source_name: National Cancer Institute — Grief, Bereavement, and Loss (PDQ)
items.source_locator: NCI PDQ — Anticipatory Grief: grief reaction occurring in anticipation of an impending loss/death and experienced by patients and family members.
items.source_version: Current NCI PDQ professional summary; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: Sadness, preparation and funeral planning before an expected death can represent anticipatory grief and should not automatically be labeled depression, denial or prolonged/complicated grief.

items.source_name: U.S. Preventive Services Task Force — Intimate Partner Violence Screening
items.source_locator: Recommendation Summary, Pathway to Benefit, and Clinician Summary: screen women of reproductive age, including pregnant/postpartum women, and provide/refer positive screens to multicomponent interventions with ongoing support.
items.source_version: USPSTF Final Recommendation published 2025-06-24, Grade B; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
items.finding: An asymptomatic 29-year-old woman falls within the population for recommended IPV screening; positive screens should be connected with appropriate multicomponent support, while reporting duties are jurisdiction/circumstance dependent.
